newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria can curb internal lending before IMF deal.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria can curb internal lending before IMF deal.

text.p: Bulgaria can tighten central bank lending as part of its implementation of a currency board mechanism before a deal with the International Monetary Fund is in place, Finance Minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said on Tuesday.
"I see no obstacles in tightening the financial discipline before the introduction of a currency board," Gavriiski told reporters.

IMF negotiators started talks with Bulgaria's interim government last week on a funding agreement linked to implementation of a fixed exchange rate mechanism to help stabilise the crumbling economy and repay foreign debts.

"At the moment we are discussing versions of a currency board mechanism and its basic parameters...the future funding programme will depend very much on what we agree on now," said Gavriiski, speaking after a meeting with the Fund.
Last week the interim cabinet said it was possible to reach a preliminary agreement with the Fund by the end of this week.
The agreement would represent the government's programme on how to solve a grave banking and currency crisis, this year's budget and structural reform plans.

The system would require levs in circulation to be matched by central bank reserves, severely curbing the financial powers of the government and the central bank and restricting the printing of money.
The programme will also contain legal amendments to bank laws designed jointly with the IMF to enable the introduction of the currency board.
Ways to resolve Bulgaria's 1.7 trillion lev domestic debt, seen as a hindrance to successful stabilisation, must also be finalised the end of the mission's work, said Gavriiski.
The amendments would need to be passed by the new parliament before the currency board is introduced after April 19 general elections.
The caretaker cabinet appointed three weeks ago has pledged to speed up privatisation aiming to boost foreign investment, shut down loss-making state companies and liberalise prices and trade rules.
Gavriiski said it was impossible to peg the lev at the moment as the rate and the currency would depend very much on the programme agreed with the Fund.
Another meeting between the IMF team and the cabinet is scheduled for Thursday.
An EU mission is expected to arrive in Sofia on March 17-18 to negotiate additional balance of payments support. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
